CONTINUITY REQUIREMENTS

Treat the continuity-bible sheet and supplied references as authoritative.

- The Hand Monster is a hand-derived creature with five digit limbs.

- The spider alive/dead state must follow the shot context.

103:

106: | Class | Use when | Deliverable |

158: 5. Replace each nonhumanoid proxy using [nonhumanoid-models.md](references/nonhumanoid-models.md), retaining a nonzero refinement log and before/after review evidence.
159: 6. Process 3–5 shots at a time under [batch-review.md](references/batch-review.md). A failed shot blocks the next batch.
160: 7. Rerender only affected outputs, verify their timestamps/revision against the latest scene change, then run the final preservation check.

166: ## Export profiles and package planning
167: 
168: Before any render, ask for the required output profile or infer it from the request and state the inference. **Never silently default to clay-only.** Use the built-in recommended `ai-control-full` profile when the task requires AI-control, multipass, clean-plate, character-only, projected, or depth deliverables. Its exact Agent plan is [ai-control-full-export-plan.json](examples/ai-control-full-export-plan.json).
169: 
170: 1. Apply the profile through `agent:apply -- --plan <path> --write`.
171: 2. Call `window.foreScene.createExportPlan()` afterward.
172: 3. Confirm every required artifact kind is planned with `disposition: "produce"`; required projected artifacts omitted with `missing-projector` are a blocking failure, not a warning to ignore.
173: 4. For a motion-required shot, verify the clay/projected/depth camera-move and reference-frame artifacts expected by the selected profile. For a still, explicitly record that motion artifacts are not required.
174: 5. Only then run `agent:package` and verify the resulting files.
175: 
176: See [deliverables.md](references/deliverables.md) for the output matrix, expected artifact kinds, and the blocking projection rule.

178: ## Batch review and visual acceptance
179: 
180: Use a default batch size of **3–5 shots**. Render review frames, inspect every frame, write a batch review, repair failures, and only then continue. A successful command or `validation.json` does not authorize the next batch. Use [batch-review.md](references/batch-review.md).
181: 
182: Visual QA is authoritative: compare the final frame with the shot description, make sure the intended subjects/framing/scene elements/replacement assets are present, and open or sample every MP4. Empty rooms, irrelevant fragments, and proxies standing in for final assets fail automatically. If visual evidence conflicts with `validation.json`, mark the shot failed. Full criteria: [visual-acceptance.md](references/visual-acceptance.md).
183: 
184: ## Command inventory
185: 
186: These commands are available in the ForeScene checkout:
187: 
188: ```bash
189: npm run agent:inspect
190: npm run agent:analyze-character
191: npm run agent:import-character
192: npm run agent:import-model
193: npm run agent:replace-proxy
194: npm run agent:render-passes
195: npm run agent:plan-exports
196: npm run agent:verify-package
197: npm run agent:preview
198: npm run agent:apply
199: npm run agent:screenshot
200: npm run agent:frame
201: npm run agent:video
202: npm run agent:verify
203: npm run agent:run
204: npm run agent:previs
205: npm run agent:render-stills
206: npm run agent:contact-sheet
207: npm run agent:package
208: ```
209: 
210: Use `agent:frame` for clean clay samples and `agent:video` for a direct shot render. `agent:previs` is a Greenfield manifest orchestration command; it is not the default replacement path for an existing project.
211: 
212: The commands above remain independently available primitives.
213: 
214: Optional advanced runner (not a primitive):
215: 
216: ```bash
217: npm run agent:refine
218: ```
219: 
220: Use this only for high-risk, resumable modification of a valuable existing project; do not route an ordinary existing-project workflow through it by default.
221: 
222: ## Artifact layout and evidence
223: 
224: ```text
225: artifacts/previs/
226: ├── preflight/
227: │   ├── project-preservation.json
228: │   └── project-preservation-final.json
229: ├── reviews/
230: │   └── batch-01.json
231: ├── refinement/
232: │   └── nonhumanoid-replacements.json
233: ├── shots/
234: │   ├── 010.png
235: │   ├── 010.composition.json
236: │   └── 010.mp4
237: ├── contact-sheet.png
238: ├── contact-sheet.html
239: ├── review/
240: │   ├── location-*.png
241: │   ├── motion-triptych-*.png (when motion samples are supplied)
242: │   └── continuity-*.png
243: ├── package.zip
244: ├── validation.json
245: ├── summary.json
246: └── run-state.json
247: ```
248: 
249: `shots/*.png` must come from the canonical clean clay renderer (`window.foreScene.renderShotFrame`), not a UI screenshot. `debug/*-ui.png` is for human debugging only. A contact sheet is required for readable review but cannot replace opening suspicious individual frames.
250: 
251: The production review planner supports a master sequence sheet,
252: location-grouped sheets, motion triptychs, and adjacent-shot continuity strips.
253: The runner emits motion triptychs when event-aware motion samples are supplied;
254: otherwise it emits the available still-based sheets under `review/`.
255: Use `logs/production-review-artifacts.json` to read each tile's shot identity,
256: sample time, presence/panorama/composition diagnostics, review status, and cache
257: state. Treat these sheets as compact evidence for review; route any repair
258: proposal through a previewed, verified mutation and record the resulting review
259: decision separately.
260: 
261: For every motion shot, render and inspect `t = 0`, `t = duration / 2`, and `t = duration`; open or sample the MP4 itself. Confirm the MP4 exists, is nonempty, matches the shot/pass identity, and is newer than the relevant scene change.
262: 
263: ## Agent browser APIs
264: 
265: Useful when inspecting a live session:
266: 
267: - `window.foreScene.getProjectDocument()` — read-only full project snapshot for preservation IDs.
268: - `window.foreScene.createExportPlan({ shotIds? })` — package plan that must be checked before rendering.
269: - `window.foreScene.renderShotFrame({ shotId, timeSeconds, pass: 'clay' })` — clean clay PNG data URL and pixel stats.
270: - `window.foreScene.waitForViewportReady({ workspace: 'shots', shotId })` — stable visual readiness, not just idle.
271: - `window.foreScene.waitForIdle()` — busy flags only; not proof that the viewport is visually ready.
272: 
273: Wait for idle before starting another package, graybox, character-import, or video operation. Never overlap Agent writes.
274: 
275: ## Rules
276: 
277: - Cast entries may use `type: "human_dummy"` or `type: "imported_character"`. Imported entries declare a local `source` and `rigMode` (for example `preserve-existing`); `agent:previs` resolves the source, analyzes it, imports it, and records the live object under `cast.<id>` before compiling shots. See [imported-characters.md](references/imported-characters.md).
278: - Use the closest supported location, camera, and pose templates. Do not invent coordinates before compilation; derive conservative relative changes from the inspected project.
279: - Let ForeScene repair numeric distance, headroom, recentering, OTS shoulder side, and related geometry only after the creative selection is correct. Numeric validation never overrides a visual failure.
280: - Never use `debug/*-ui.png` as production-frame evidence.
281: - Derive final claims from verified artifact and review records only. See [error-recovery.md](references/error-recovery.md) for the required honest summary.

1: # Previs Production Manifest
2: 
3: Versioned semantic input for autonomous graybox previs.
4: 
5: Grok Build makes **semantic** decisions (locations, cast, shot size, blocking).
6: ForeScene compiles those decisions into geometry and Agent API plans.
7: 
8: ```
9: shotlist.md
10:   → PrevisProductionManifestV1
11:   → ForeScene deterministic compiler
12:   → Existing Agent API plans (preview / apply / undo)
13:   → Clay first-frame PNGs + contact sheet
14: ```
15: 
16: ## Schema
17: 
18: `version` must be `1`.
19: 
20: ```ts
21: interface PrevisProductionManifestV1 {
22:   version: 1;
23:   project: {
24:     name: string;
25:     description?: string;
26:     aspectRatio: '16:9' | '9:16' | '1:1' | '2.39:1';
27:     frameRate?: number;
28:   };
29:   locations: PrevisLocationDefinition[];
30:   cast: PrevisCharacterDefinition[];
31:   props?: PrevisPropDefinition[];
32:   shots: PrevisShotDefinition[];
33: }
34: ```
35: 
36: Cast entries may be built-in semantic mannequins or imported characters. An
37: imported character source is resolved relative to the manifest file, analyzed,
38: and imported through the existing Agent character-import path during the same
39: `agent:previs` cast phase. The normalized cast ID is then used by every shot,
40: so no second staging command or manual object-ID lookup is required.
41: 
42: ```json
43: {
44:   "id": "joseph",
45:   "type": "imported_character",
46:   "source": "./characters/joseph.glb",
47:   "rigMode": "preserve-existing"
48: }
49: ```
50: 
51: `name` is optional for imported entries and defaults to the cast ID. Supported
52: `rigMode` values are `preserve-existing`, `auto`, `autorig`, and `saved-rig`.
53: `source` must be a local GLB, embedded glTF, or FBX file. A missing source or
54: failed rig analysis stops the cast phase without advancing shot compilation;
55: successful imports are retained in `run-state.json` under `cast.<id>` for retry
56: recovery.
57: 
58: Use `saved-rig` when the source model and its matching ForeScene rig package
59: must be imported as one cast entry:
60: 
61: ```json
62: {
63:   "id": "joseph",
64:   "type": "imported_character",
65:   "source": "./characters/joseph.glb",
66:   "rigMode": "saved-rig",
67:   "rigPackage": "./characters/joseph.fsrig",
68:   "height": 1.8
69: }
70: ```
71: 
72: `rigPackage` is required only for `saved-rig` and must be an explicit local
73: `.fsrig` or legacy `.panorig` path relative to the manifest. The package and
74: source are preflighted read-only before an authorized project reset; topology,
75: vertex-count, skin/bind, and preserved-skeleton mismatches stop the run before
76: reset or shot compilation. The package is then applied through the same shared
77: import path used by the Build tray, with package assets cleaned up on failure.
78: Changing either file or the import options changes the cast fingerprint. Resume
79: reuses a cast mapping only when that fingerprint still matches; otherwise run
80: with `--update-manifest --reset-project` to rebuild the cast-dependent scene.
81: Heavy or extreme character imports are refused unless the run explicitly opts
82: in with `--allow-heavy-character-imports`; the flag supplies the same non-empty
83: consent token used by the direct Agent import API.
84: 
85: Shots may include optional temporal authoring. It is compiled into the same
86: Agent timeline commands used by direct automation, so it participates in plan
87: preview, atomic apply, undo, and controlled invalidation of stale video assets:
88: 
89: ```json
90: {
91:   "motion": {
92:     "durationSeconds": 4,
93:     "renderControlVideo": true,
94:     "keyframes": [
95:       { "timeSeconds": 0, "camera": { "position": [0, 2, 6], "target": [0, 1, 0] } },
96:       { "timeSeconds": 4, "camera": { "position": [2, 2, 4], "target": [0, 1, 0] },
97:         "staging": [{ "subject": "alex", "transform": { "position": [1, 0, 0] } }] }
98:     ]
99:   }
100: }
101: ```
102: 
103: Motion requires at least two strictly increasing keyframes, with the final
104: keyframe time equal to `durationSeconds`. When `renderControlVideo` is `true`,
105: `agent:previs` performs a deterministic 1080p clay camera-move render after
106: the shot is compiled, attaches it to the shot, and saves the MP4 under the
107: run output's `shots/` directory. The render is skipped when that artifact is
108: already present in resumable run-state.
109: 
110: See `src/engine/previs/manifest.ts` for the full TypeScript contract.
111: 
112: ## Location templates
113: 
114: Built-in templates (MVP):
115: 
116: | Template | Use |
117: |----------|-----|
118: | `empty_stage` | Neutral open stage |
119: | `interior_room` | Simple dialogue room |
120: | `corridor` | Narrow hall |
121: | `ruins` | Roman ruins courtyard |
122: | `armory` | Armory interior |
123: | `exterior_courtyard` | Open courtyard |
124: | `custom_blueprint` | Reserved — rejected in MVP |
125: 
126: Each location is placed in a separate zone origin: `[index * 100, 0, 0]`.
127: Templates generate named anchors (`center`, `entrance`, `exit`, …).
128: 
129: ## Pose presets
130: 
131: Accepted semantic poses:
132: 
133: `standing-neutral`, `standing-alert`, `standing-defensive`, `walking`, `running`,
134: `kneeling`, `seated`, `reaching`, `holding-object`, `shield-ready`, `sword-ready`, `injured`
135: 
136: Prepared production projects may persist typed bindings and shot contracts under
137: `workflow.production` (project schema `1.2`). A contract can bind an entity to
138: an object or complete object group, require pose/deformation capabilities, and
139: record an exact dynamic-presence set before compilation. Use the browser Agent
140: API to inspect and validate these gates:
141: 
142: ```ts
143: window.foreScene.inspectEntityCapability({ entityId: 'lead' });
144: window.foreScene.validateProductionCapabilities({ manifest });
145: window.foreScene.resolveProductionPose({
146:   entityId: 'lead',
147:   requestedPose: 'running',
148:   shotId: 'shot-001',
149: });
150: ```
151: 
152: Native presets resolve as `exact`. Semantic fallbacks such as `running` → a
153: single walking-contact pose are reported as `approximate` and require review;
154: they are not treated as production-approved substitutions until an explicit
155: `approvePoseSubstitution` record is persisted. A rig marked `requiresRerigging`
156: or missing required joints blocks pose-dependent shots, while static geometry
157: may still satisfy a static-only contract.
158: 
159: Environment contracts route a shot to a prepared location panorama. The
160: location must name `defaultPanoId` or `panoIds`; the compiler emits an
161: executable `shot.setPanorama` command and verification compares the resulting
162: shot link against the expected ID:
163: 
164: ```ts
165: window.foreScene.inspectShotEnvironmentContract({ shotId: 'shot-001' });
166: window.foreScene.verifyShotPanorama({ shotId: 'shot-001' });
167: ```
168: 
169: When `requireProjection` is enabled, projected approval uses a WebGL coverage
170: debug pass. `inspectProjectionHealth` reports projected-material count,
171: panorama coverage, fallback ratio, and whether an occlusion map was available;
172: a linked panorama ID by itself is not a projection-health result.
173: 
174: ```ts
175: await window.foreScene.inspectProjectionHealth({
176:   shotId: 'shot-001',
177:   timeSeconds: 0,
178: });
179: ```
180: 
181: ## Reference-driven composition
182: 
183: An external storyboard or layout review may be reduced to normalized screen-space
184: facts without putting image understanding in ForeScene. The contract can name
185: subject and prop bounds, head/face points, screen regions, expected coverage,
186: horizon/floor lines, and intentional foreground/background overlap:
187: 
188: ```ts
189: await window.foreScene.setShotCompositionConstraints({
190:   shotId: 'shot-001',
191:   contract: {
192:     referenceImageAssetId: 'storyboard-001',
193:     subjects: [{
194:       entityId: 'lead',
195:       expectedBounds: { x: 0.32, y: 0.18, width: 0.28, height: 0.68 },
196:       headPoint: [0.46, 0.2],
197:       screenRegion: 'center',
198:     }],
199:     cropTolerance: 0.05,
200:   },
201: });
202: window.foreScene.inspectShotCompositionError({ shotId: 'shot-001' });
203: window.foreScene.verifyShotCompositionConstraints({ shotId: 'shot-001' });
204: await window.foreScene.solveShotToCompositionConstraints({ shotId: 'shot-001' });
205: ```
206: 
207: The deterministic solver may adjust only camera position, target, and FOV. It
208: does not swap entities, alter poses or continuity state, change location, or
209: replace assets. A saved composition contract is a hard first-frame gate, so a
210: generic framing percentage is not enough when the approved reference places a
211: subject elsewhere. Failed solves are not committed; inspect and repair the
212: contract or the prepared asset before proceeding.
213: 
214: ## Verified mutations
215: 
216: Mutations whose semantic result matters use a recovery checkpoint plus a
217: postcondition check. The proxy-replacement adapter is available through:
218: 
219: ```ts
220: await window.foreScene.applyVerifiedProxyReplacement({
221:   proxyObjectId: 'proxy-lead',
222:   replacementObjectId: 'lead-import',
223:   requestedShotIds: ['shot-001'],
224:   intendedShotIds: ['shot-001', 'shot-002'],
225:   initializeVisibility: true,
226: });
227: ```
228: 
229: The result includes the preview, atomic apply result, verification report, and
230: rollback report. A failed replacement is restored automatically to the
231: checkpoint, including unaffected shot state; `restoreRefinementCheckpoint`
232: remains available for an explicit operator rollback. Refinement batches also
233: automatically restore their batch checkpoint after a blocking verification or
234: review failure, leaving the batch pending for retry.
235: 
236: ## Production gates and canary
237: 
238: Production orchestration is a gated state machine. Input, bindings, and asset
239: capabilities are validated before a recovery revision and a small canary are
240: authored. The canary uses a deterministic greedy set-cover over location,
241: panorama, imported-character, pose, multipart, prop, visibility, camera-motion,
242: and reference-composition capabilities. It emits only clay-with-subjects,
243: characters-only, clean-plate, and (when required) projected-with-subjects
244: review outputs.
245: 
246: ```ts
247: const planned = window.foreScene.planProductionCanary({ manifest });
248: const canary = window.foreScene.runProductionCanary({
249:   runId: planned.runId!,
250:   results: observedCanaryResults,
251: });
252: await window.foreScene.approveProductionCanary({ runId: planned.runId! });
253: window.foreScene.inspectProductionGates({ runId: planned.runId });
254: ```
255: 
256: The full still sequence remains locked until canary presence, capability,
257: panorama, composition, unrelated-state, and output checks pass. A failed
258: canary can only be overridden with a non-empty reason, which is retained in the
259: gate report. Command success and artifact existence do not constitute visual
260: approval.
261: 
262: Still approval is a separate gate. After the full still sequence has passed
263: verification, approval records the exact project fingerprint and reviewed
264: shot/artifact IDs on a verified revision:
265: 
266: ```ts
267: await window.foreScene.approveStillLayout({
268:   runId: planned.runId!,
269:   approvedShotIds: ['shot-001', 'shot-002'],
270:   reviewArtifactIds: ['master-sheet'],
271:   reviewRecord: 'Primary still layout approved for motion blocking.',
272: });
273: const motion = await window.foreScene.createMotionWorkingRevision({
274:   runId: planned.runId!,
275: });
276: ```
277: 
278: Motion work is cloned into a separate persisted revision and never loads over
279: the approved still revision. If the approved project fingerprint or an
280: approved shot's camera, staging, pose, visibility, or panorama changes, the
281: motion branch is rejected as stale.
282: 
283: ## Cached review and adaptive sampling
284: 
285: Review frames are keyed by renderer version, profile, effective camera and
286: staging at the sample time, linked panorama/style settings, relevant asset
287: content hashes, and prepared-location revision. The run-state stores that key;
288: an existing PNG is reused only when the current project produces the same key.
289: Changing an unrelated dynamic object therefore does not invalidate every shot,
290: while changing a camera, pose, panorama, or relevant location object does.
291: 
292: ```ts
293: window.foreScene.planReviewSamples({
294:   shotId: 'shot-001',
295:   strategy: 'event-aware',
296:   maxSamples: 3,
297: });
298: ```
299: 
300: Static shots plan one sample. Linear camera moves plan start/end; direction
301: changes and visibility/pose events are preferred within the configured bound.
302: Motion review remains sample-based until still approval; it does not imply a
303: video or complete pass matrix.
304: 
305: Browser callers can inspect and invalidate the persisted cache without changing
306: the project:
307: 
308: ```ts
309: window.foreScene.inspectRenderCache();
310: window.foreScene.explainRenderCacheHit({ fingerprint });
311: window.foreScene.invalidateRenderDependencies({ dependencyIds: ['object:obj-1'] });
312: ```
313: 
314: ## Project-wide review artifacts
315: 
316: The production review planner groups the same canonical frames into compact,
317: readable artifacts:
318: 
319: - a master sequence sheet;
320: - one sheet per prepared location;
321: - motion triptychs using event-aware samples when motion frames are supplied; and
322: - adjacent-shot continuity strips.
323: 
324: Every tile carries the shot number/name, sample time, location, camera recipe,
325: presence and panorama status, composition error when measured, review status,
326: diagnostic badges, and cache-hit state. These are review evidence, not approval
327: records. External visual feedback is normalized into repair intents and must be
328: applied through previewed, verified mutations.
329: 
330: The CLI writes the master sheet at `contact-sheet.png` and the grouped sheets
331: under `review/`; `logs/production-review-artifacts.json` is the machine-readable
332: index. No sheet or artifact-existence check is itself a visual approval.
333: 
334: The same pure planner is available to browser callers when frames already live
335: in the Agent artifact registry:
336: 
337: ```ts
338: window.foreScene.planProductionReviewArtifacts({ frames });
339: ```
340: 
341: ## Browser-owned production runs
342: 
343: The browser Agent API persists lifecycle state independently of the Node CLI,
344: including the current gate, completed shot IDs, cache keys, artifact handles,
345: blocking diagnostics, and explicit overrides. A restart can inspect the same
346: run and resume only after the outstanding approval gate is satisfied:
347: 
348: ```ts
349: const run = await window.foreScene.runProduction({ manifest });
350: window.foreScene.subscribeProductionRun(run.runId, (state) => console.log(state.currentGate, state.status));
351: window.foreScene.getProductionRun(run.runId);
352: await window.foreScene.resumeProductionRun(run.runId);
353: ```
354: 
355: `pauseProductionRun`, `resumeProductionRun`, and `cancelProductionRun` are
356: stateful lifecycle operations. Cancellation preserves completed verified
357: artifacts; it does not roll back the project unless a blocking mutation gate
358: requires rollback.
359: 
360: ## Camera templates
361: 
362: `establishing`, `wide`, `full`, `medium`, `medium_close_up`, `close_up`,
363: `extreme_close_up`, `two_shot`, `over_the_shoulder`, `insert`, `profile`,
364: `low_angle`, `high_angle`, `overhead`
365: 
366: - `two_shot` requires ≥2 `camera.subjects`
367: - `over_the_shoulder` requires `camera.foregroundSubject`
368: 
369: Shot numbers from the manifest are preserved exactly (`shotNumber` / `productionShotId`).
370: 
371: ## CLI
372: 
373: ```bash
374: # Initialize / reset only
375: npm run agent:previs -- \
376:   --manifest examples/previs/minimal-dialogue.json \
377:   --url http://127.0.0.1:3000 \
378:   --write \
379:   --reset-project \
380:   --initialize-only \
381:   --output artifacts/previs
382: 
383: # Full orchestration
384: npm run agent:previs -- \
385:   --manifest examples/previs/music-video-graybox.json \
386:   --url https://forescene.app \
387:   --write \
388:   --reset-project \
389:   --output artifacts/previs
390: ```
391: 
392: Add `--allow-heavy-character-imports` when the manifest intentionally includes
393: a character above the standard memory tier.
394: 
395: Safety:
396: 
397: - `--write` alone does **not** authorize project replacement
398: - `--reset-project` must be passed together with `--write`
399: - Manifest hash is stored in `run-state.json`; resume refuses a silently changed manifest
400: - Pass `--update-manifest` to accept a changed manifest and invalidate only affected shots (and dependents). Shot-only edits resume without `--reset-project`; location/cast/prop edits also need `--reset-project`
401: - `--profile` selects a persistent Playwright user-data directory
402: - Unless `--skip-package` is set, a failed package phase makes the run `ok: false`
403: 
404: Live Chromium coverage: `npm run test:e2e:previs` (tagged `@heavy`).
405: 
406: ## Output layout
407: 
408: ```
409: artifacts/previs/
410: ├── manifest.normalized.json
411: ├── run-state.json
412: ├── validation.json
413: ├── summary.json
414: ├── contact-sheet.png
415: ├── package.zip
416: ├── logs/
417: └── shots/
418:     ├── 010.png
419:     └── …
420: ```

1: # ForeScene Agent API
2: 
3: ForeScene exposes a browser Agent API on `window.foreScene` so CLI coding agents can inspect and mutate the open project without clicking through the UI.
4: 
5: Playwright hosts and observes the browser. The Agent API performs exact project reads and protected mutations.
6:

17: **Milestone 9 — temporal authoring and controlled video** ✓

19: Available now:
20: 
21: - Inspection, preview, atomic apply/undo
22: - Shot staging, landmarks, export configuration patches
23: - Package export via API / CLI / Agent Console
24: - `npm run agent:screenshot` / `agent:verify` / `agent:run` / `agent:package`
25: - Project menu → **Agent Console** (same `window.foreScene` path)
26: - Timeline inspection and arbitrary-time sampling without changing the live shot
27: - Declarative timeline replacement, keyframe create/update/delete, staging, preview/apply, and undo
28: - Multipass still review via `renderShotFrame({ shotId, appearance, peopleVariant, content })`
29: - Controlled shot video rendering with progress and cancellation via `renderShotVideo()`
30: - `getShotDocument({ id })` for exact shot staging/keyframe inspection
31: - `importModel({ file })` for the same protected geometry import used by the manual dialog
32: 
33: ## Quick start
34: 
35: ```bash
36: npm run dev
37: npm run agent:inspect
38: ```
39: 
40: JSON is written to stdout. Diagnostics and progress go to stderr.
41: 
42: ## Permission model
43: 
44: Agent control mode is an **accidental-write guard**, not a security boundary against hostile page scripts (those already own the origin).
45: 
46: | Mode | Inspection | Mutations / package export |
47: |------|------------|----------------------------|
48: | `off` | blocked | blocked |
49: | `read-only` (default) | allowed | blocked (`write_access_required`) |
50: | `read-write` | allowed | allowed |
51: 
52: **Escalation** (grant writes) is deliberate only:
53: 
54: - Project menu → **Enable Agent Writes**, or Agent Console toggle (UI → Zustand store)
55: - CLI `--write` → sessionStorage seed for this tab only
56: - CLI `--persist-write` → localStorage seed for a trusted persistent profile
57: 
58: **Demotion** is available to every caller:
59: 
60: - Header **Stop**, Project menu **Disable Agent Writes**, Agent Console toggle
61: - `window.foreScene.disableWrites()` (never grants `read-write`)
62: 
63: CLI launches always clear a stale localStorage write seed unless `--persist-write` is present. `apply` / `run` / `package` refuse to start without an explicit `--write` or `--persist-write`.
64: 
65: ## Model import
66: 
67: `importModel({ file, mode })` uses the shared model conversion and local-recovery
68: commit path behind **Import 3D scene**. It creates texture-free graybox geometry,
69: registers its binary payloads, and adds the resulting objects in the same protected
70: project mutation. It requires `read-write` access. Heavy geometry returns a
71: structured `requiresConsent` result until its caller sends the explicit
72: `allow-heavy-model-imports` token; extreme imports also require the literal
73: `IMPORT` confirmation.
74: 
75: `getShotDocument({ id })` returns a structured copy of the requested `Shot`,
76: including `objectOverrides` and `cameraKeyframes`. Use it when a workflow must
77: copy exact staging rather than infer it from summary inspection fields.
78:

80:

105: ## Agent API v1 improvements
106: 
107: ### Shot panorama
108: 
109: ```ts
110: await foreScene.setShotPanorama({ shotId, panoId: 'pano_…' });
111: await foreScene.setShotPanorama({ shotId, panoId: null }); // unlink
112: ```
113: 
114: Atomically updates `linkedPanoId`, `panoCrop`, active panorama state, and persistence.
115: 
116: ### Render / export result contract
117: 
118: Render and export operations now return a stable `status` plus optional `artifact`:
119: 
120: | `status` | Meaning |
121: |----------|---------|
122: | `completed` | Artifact produced, no quality issues |
123: | `completed_with_warnings` | Artifact produced; inspect `diagnostics` |
124: | `failed` | No usable artifact |
125: | `stale_revision` | Project changed during render |
126: | `cancelled` / `busy` | Operation did not complete |
127: 
128: `ok` is `true` when `status` is `completed` or `completed_with_warnings` — a frame with `frame_zero_variance` still returns the PNG in `artifact` / `pngDataUrl`.
129: 
130: ### Artifact handles
131: 
132: Video render, package export, and project backup register blobs in-memory:
133: 
134: ```ts
135: const video = await foreScene.renderShotVideo({ shotId, download: false });
136: const bytes = await foreScene.downloadArtifact({ artifactId: video.artifact!.artifactId });
137: const backup = await foreScene.exportProjectBackup({ download: false });
138: ```
139: 
140: ### Discovery
141: 
142: ```ts
143: foreScene.describeCapabilities();
144: foreScene.describeOperation('setShotPanorama');
145: foreScene.getAgentSchema();
146: ```
147: 
148: CLI: `npm run agent:help -- --json`
149: 
150: ### Spatial primitives
151: 
152: All spatial primitives are **shot-scoped** — they read shot-effective transforms and write sparse `shot.objectOverrides` (never base `scene.objects`).
153: 
154: `snapObjectToFloor({ shotId, object })`, `placeObjectNearLandmark`, `frameSubjects`, `orientObjectToward`, and `trackSubjects` follow this model.
155: 
156: `trackSubjects` samples subject transforms at `startTime` and `endTime`, solves distinct cameras, and warns when subject displacement is negligible or the cameras are identical. Tracking inserts or updates keyframes at the requested times without rescaling existing timeline timing.
157: 
158: ### Timeline helpers
159: 
160: `sampleShotState`, `captureShotStateAsKeyframe`, and `upsertObjectKeyframe` preserve explicit staging at timeline times.
161: 
162: ### Shot diagnostics
163: 
164: `inspectShotDiagnostics({ shotId, timeSeconds?, subjectIds? })` returns diagnostics for explicitly requested objects of any type, or infers likely subjects when `subjectIds` is omitted.
165: 
166: Per-subject fields:
167: 
168: - `screenCoverage` — projected frame occupancy
169: - `visibleFraction` — in-frame visible subject fraction (`visibleArea / unclippedArea * (1 - occlusionRatio)`)
170: - `groundClearanceMeters` — signed distance to identified floor (negative = below floor)
171: - `behindCamera`, `clipped`, `occlusionRatio`
172: - `humanLandmarks` — optional head/body landmarks for humanoid objects
173: 
174: Shot-level fields:
175: - `cameraIntersectsSolidGeometry` — camera inside a wall/box/column
176: - `cameraInsideEnvironmentBounds` — camera inside inferred navigable envelope
177: - `linkedPanoramaResolved` — panorama link resolves (not a render confirmation)
178: - `cameraDisplacementMeters` and `subjectDisplacements`
179: 
180: ### Revision sync
181: 
182: Every mutation returns `revisionId`. Call `refreshRevision()` before retrying after `stale_revision`.
183: 
184: ## Export planning
185: 
186: `createExportPlan({ shotIds?: string[] })` calls the same pure `createExportPlan()` engine used by the Export workspace. It does not render or download anything.
187: 
188: When `shotIds` is omitted, every shot is planned (matching the Export workspace default selection).
189: 
190: Use the CLI when a review workflow needs a persisted preflight plan and a
191: post-export archive check:
192: 
193: ```bash
194: npm run agent:plan-exports -- --shots 01,02,03 --output artifacts/preflight/deliverables-plan.json
195: npm run agent:verify-package -- \
196:   --plan artifacts/preflight/deliverables-plan.json \
197:   --package artifacts/package.zip
198: ```
199: 
200: `agent:verify-package` reads the ZIP and requires every file from every
201: `produce` artifact in the recorded export plan. It reports each missing entry
202: with its shot and artifact kind, so a requested projected, clean-plate,
203: character-only, or depth pass cannot silently disappear from delivery.
204: 
205: ## Multipass still review
206: 
207: `renderShotFrame` uses the same render paths as package export without writing
208: assets or changing the live shot. `appearance` is `clay`, `projected`, or
209: `depth`; `peopleVariant` is `with_people` or `clean_plate`; and `content` is
210: `full_scene` or `characters_only`. Character-only is a transparent pass with
211: the environment removed. Depth results include linear camera-depth metadata and
212: the sampled grayscale ratio. Projected requests fail with a clear diagnostic
213: when no valid styled panorama/projector is available.
214: 
215: ```bash
216: npm run agent:render-passes -- \
217:   --shots 01,02,03,04 \
218:   --output artifacts/reviews/batch-01
219: ```
220: 
221: This writes six deterministic files per shot — clay with characters, clay clean
222: plate, projected with characters, projected clean plate, characters only, and
223: depth — plus `review-manifest.json`. The manifest records each renderer source,
224: pixel/depth inspection data, and a SHA-256 for comparison before packaging.
225: `agent:refine` adds a `temporal` record for every renderable camera move to
226: that same manifest:
227: 
228: ```json
229: {
230:   "temporal": {
231:     "renderable": true,
232:     "start": { "output": "temporal/start.png", "sha256": "sha256:..." },
233:     "mid": { "output": "temporal/mid.png", "sha256": "sha256:..." },
234:     "end": { "output": "temporal/end.png", "sha256": "sha256:..." },
235:     "video": {
236:       "output": "temporal/motion-preview.mp4",
237:       "sha256": "sha256:...",
238:       "durationSeconds": 3
239:     }
240:   }
241: }
242: ```
243: 
244: Semantic approval must include a generic criterion result for every criterion
245: listed by the manifest. Renderable shots include `temporal.motion` and must
246: pass it; non-renderable shots do not receive that criterion. Every still and
247: temporal artifact must also appear in `reviewedArtifacts` with its matching
248: SHA-256.
249: 
250: ## Existing-project refinement
251: 
252: `agent:refine` is intentionally separate from the greenfield previs manifest.
253: It captures a durable preservation baseline before the first mutation, then
254: permits one batch at a time. The baseline protects project, shot, panorama,
255: existing-object, camera, and timeline identities; import/replacement work may
256: add objects and alter only the required staging overrides.
257: 
258: ```json
259: {
260:   "version": 2,
261:   "mode": "existing-project-refinement",
262:   "preserve": {
263:     "project": true, "shots": true, "panoramas": true,
264:     "environmentObjects": true, "cameras": true, "timelines": true
265:   },
266:   "allowMutations": {
267:     "shotStaging": [], "pose": [], "camera": [], "timeline": [], "visibility": []
268:   },
269:   "characterImports": [
270:     { "id": "subject-variant-a", "batchId": "batch-01", "file": "production/<production-id>/subject-variant-a.glb", "rigPackage": "production/<production-id>/subject-variant-a.fsrig", "rigMode": "saved-rig" }
271:   ],
272:   "modelImports": [
273:     { "id": "replacement-object-a", "batchId": "batch-01", "file": "production/<production-id>/replacement-object-a.glb", "mode": "combined" }
274:   ],
275:   "characterAssignments": [
276:     { "id": "assign-subject-a", "importId": "subject-variant-a", "replaceObjectId": "existing-subject-placeholder", "shots": ["01"] }
277:   ],
278:   "proxyReplacements": [
279:     { "id": "replace-object-a", "batchId": "batch-01", "proxyObjectId": "proxy-object-a", "replacementImportId": "replacement-object-a", "shots": ["01"] }
280:   ],
281:   "batches": [{ "id": "batch-01", "shots": ["01"] }],
282:   "deliverablesProfile": "ai-control-full",
283:   "reviewPolicy": { "additionalCriteria": [], "shotRequirements": [] },
284:   "finalization": { "scope": "reviewed_shots" },
285:   "subjectObjectIds": []
286: }
287: ```
288: 
289: Run a batch, complete a semantic visual review, approve it explicitly, then
290: advance or finalize:
291: 
292: ```bash
293: npm run agent:refine -- --plan production/refinement-plan.json --batch batch-01 --write --output artifacts/refinement
294: npm run agent:refine -- --plan production/refinement-plan.json --approve batch-01 --review artifacts/refinement/reviews/batch-01.semantic.json --output artifacts/refinement
295: npm run agent:refine -- --plan production/refinement-plan.json --finalize --write --output artifacts/refinement
296: ```
297: 
298: A batch ends in `awaiting_visual_review` only if every required still pass,
299: temporal sample (for motion shots), and preservation check succeeds. The next
300: batch is blocked until `--approve` receives a semantic review file. It must
301: pass every shot, provide a concrete reason for every manifest criterion, and
302: include the SHA-256 of every reviewed pass and temporal artifact. Allowed
303: camera or timeline changes add the `refinement.authorized-change` criterion.
304: Finalization applies `deliverablesProfile`
305: (`ai-control-full`) before creating the export plan, then rejects missing
306: required clay, projected, clean-plate, cast, depth, or renderable-motion
307: artifacts. The planner emits one artifact per viewport pass containing both
308: people variants, and finalization validates those filenames inside the shared
309: artifact. Character still output is also produced as a transparent image for a
310: cast-free shot, keeping the package pass matrix predictable. `--profile`
311: selects only the persistent Playwright browser directory, never a deliverables
312: profile. Use `--retry batch-id` to restore a failed batch's starting revision
313: and run it again, or `--rollback batch-id` to restore without rerunning.
314: Finalization refuses
315: unapproved batches, failed/missing replacement work, visible proxies, any
316: preservation drift, or a package that omits a planned artifact.
317: 
318: Refinement finalization defaults to `scope: "reviewed_shots"` and exports the
319: deduplicated shot ids stored on approved batch state. Set
320: `finalization.scope` to `"entire_project"` to require an approved review for
321: every project shot; missing and extra reviewed ids are reported explicitly.
322: The finalization report records `reviewedShotIds`, `plannedShotIds`,
323: `exportedShotIds`, `unreviewedExportedShotIds`, `reviewedButUnexportedShotIds`,
324: and `productionComplete`. Direct export API calls reject unknown, duplicate,
325: or explicitly empty `shotIds` selections.
326: 
327: Approval also stores an `approval-record.json` containing the exact manifest
328: hash, semantic-review hash, reviewed shot ids, criterion ids, and artifact
329: count. Approval recomputes the manifest and semantic hashes and reads every
330: still and temporal output from disk; finalization repeats those checks before
331: it can produce a package.
332: 
333: For a production copy, start from
334: `examples/refinement/six-shot-pilot.template.json`, replace every placeholder
335: object/shot id with IDs from that copied project, and run the pilot before
336: adding later production batches. It demonstrates three saved-rig subject
337: variants, two replacement objects, and a sixth motion shot. Motion shots
338: also emit start/mid/end clay frames plus a downloaded 720p MP4 preview, so
339: framing and temporal output can be reviewed together.
340: 
341: ## Preview
342: 
343: `previewPlan` works in read-only mode. It never writes the live project.
344: 
345: Supported plan commands:
346: 
347: - `project.updateInfo`
348: - `object.create` / `object.update` / `object.delete` / `object.duplicate`
349: - `shot.create` / `shot.rename` / `shot.updateDescription` / `shot.updateCamera`
350: - `shot.select` / `shot.copyStagingToNext` / `shot.stageObject` / `shot.clearStaging` / `shot.delete`
351: - `landmark.create` / `landmark.update` / `landmark.delete` / `landmark.linkObject`
352: - `shot.timeline.replace` / `shot.timeline.clear` / `shot.timeline.setDuration`
353: - `shot.keyframe.create` / `shot.keyframe.update` / `shot.keyframe.delete`
354: - `shot.keyframe.stageObject` / `shot.keyframe.clearStaging`
355: 
356: ## Temporal authoring
357: 
358: Inspection is available through `inspectShotTimeline({ shotId })` and
359: `sampleShotAtTime({ shotId, timeSeconds })`. Sampling clamps to the shot duration
360: and returns interpolated camera and object overrides; it does not persist changes.
361: 
362: ```js
363: await window.foreScene.previewPlan({
364:   version: 1,
365:   planId: 'demo-motion',
366:   commands: [{
367:     op: 'shot.timeline.replace',
368:     shot: { id: 'shot-id' },
369:     durationSeconds: 4,
370:     keyframes: [
371:       { timeSeconds: 0, camera: { position: [0, 2, 6], target: [0, 1, 0] } },
372:       { timeSeconds: 4, camera: { position: [2, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] } },
373:     ],
374:   }],
375: });
376: ```
377: 
378: The CLI exposes the same render path:
379: 
380: ```bash
381: npm run agent:frame -- --shot shot-id --time 2 --output artifacts/midpoint.png
382: npm run agent:video -- --shot shot-id --write --resolution 1080p --output artifacts/shot.mp4
383: ```
384: 
385: Video rendering is exclusive with other Agent writes, reports progress through
386: `getShotVideoRenderProgress()`, and can be stopped with
387: `cancelShotVideoRender()`. A failed or cancelled render leaves the previous shot
388: video attachment intact.
389: - `export.sceneDefaults.patch`
390: - `export.shotOverrides.patch` / `reset` / `copy` / `promote`
391: - `workspace.open` / `selection.set`
392: 
393: Plan-local `ref` values bind created entities so later commands can target them. Ambiguous name queries return `ambiguous_target` with candidate ids and abort the whole plan.
394: 
395: Optional `expectedFingerprint` (from a prior inspect/preview) rejects stale projects.
396: 
397: ## Apply and undo
398: 
399: `applyPlan` / `undoLastPlan` require read-write mode. They wait for persistence idle (`criticalWrite` / graybox / package export) before committing, then:
400: 
401: 1. Prepare the plan on a clone (same path as preview)
402: 2. Confirm the live fingerprint is unchanged
403: 3. Call `runDestructiveProjectMutation()` (pre-change recovery snapshot)
404: 4. Replace project + selection/workspace in one Zustand `setState`
405: 5. Record an in-memory history entry for `undoLastPlan()`
406: 
407: If persistence throws after the live commit, the catch path restores the exact pre-plan project and selection (no history entry).
408: 
409: `undoLastPlan()` restores the preceding project only when the current fingerprint still matches the applied result. Manual edits after apply refuse undo.
410: 
411: `listPlanHistory()` returns in-memory `{ planId, description }` entries for the Agent Console.
412: 
413: ## Shot staging
414: 
415: Supported shot commands:
416: 
417: - `shot.create` / `shot.rename` / `shot.updateDescription` / `shot.updateCamera`
418: - `shot.select` / `shot.copyStagingToNext`
419: - `shot.stageObject` (transform, visible, humanPose, posePreset)
420: - `shot.clearStaging` (`clearPoseOnly` keeps transform/visibility)
421: - `shot.delete` (refuses to delete the last remaining shot)
422: 
423: Staging never mutates Build scene objects. Absolute overrides are idempotent.
424: 
425: ## Landmarks & export configuration
426: 
427: Landmark commands mutate `project.landmarks` and clean `shot.landmarkIds` on delete. `landmark.linkObject` sets/clears `linkedObjectId` after resolving the object target.
428: 
429: Export configuration commands reuse `exportConfiguration.ts`:
430: 
431: - `export.sceneDefaults.patch` → `patchSceneExportDefaults`
432: - `export.shotOverrides.patch` → `setShotExportOverride`
433: - `export.shotOverrides.reset` → full reset or one `field` path
434: - `export.shotOverrides.copy` / `promote`
435: 
436: ## Package export
437: 
438: ```ts
439: await window.foreScene.exportPackage({ shotIds?: string[], download?: true });
440: window.foreScene.getPackageExportProgress();
441: window.foreScene.cancelPackageExport();
442: ```
443: 
444: Flow matches Export workspace: wait idle → flush verified revision → `createExportPlan` → reject blocking errors → `buildMultiShotPackage` → optional `downloadBlob`. Requires read-write.
445: 
446: `download: false` is build-only: returns the package metadata without downloading and without marking shots exported.
447: 
448: ```bash
449: npm run agent:package -- --write --output artifacts/package.zip
450: npm run agent:package -- --write --shot <shotId> --output artifacts/one-shot.zip
451: ```
452: 
453: ## Agent Console
454: 
455: Project menu → **Agent Console** opens an in-app dialog that calls the same `window.foreScene` methods (preview / apply / undo / export / cancel). Enabling writes uses the UI store path; disabling uses `disableWrites()`.
456: 
457: ## Character import
458: 
459: Character analysis and import are exposed through the Agent API and appear in capability reporting as `characterImport`. The CLI stages the file through a browser file input, so binary model bytes are not serialized through `page.evaluate` arguments:
460: 
461: ```bash
462: npm run agent:analyze-character -- --file path/to/actor.glb
463: npm run agent:import-character -- --file path/to/actor.glb --rig-mode auto --write
464: npm run agent:analyze-character -- --file path/to/actor.glb --rig-package path/to/actor.fsrig --rig-mode saved-rig --output artifacts/preflight/actor.json
465: npm run agent:import-character -- --file path/to/actor.glb --rig-package path/to/actor.fsrig --rig-mode saved-rig --name "Actor" --allow-heavy-character-imports --write
466: ```
467: 
468: Auto mode preserves an existing rig only when the analysis reports skeleton and skinning data, no required mappings are missing, and mapping confidence is at least 0.7; otherwise it selects autorig. `saved-rig` stages both binary inputs, validates the package and source topology before writing, then applies the shared saved-rig importer. Results include GLB, rig-package, and combined fingerprints; a repeated exact pair reuses the existing character instead of creating a duplicate. Large imports use the device-aware model-import budget and require explicit consent (`--allow-heavy-character-imports` or `--consent-token`). Character imports participate in `waitForIdle` and block plan, reset, package, and video operations until they finish or are cancelled.
469: 
470: ## Ordinary model import and proxy replacement
471: 
472: ```bash
473: npm run agent:import-model -- --file input/model.glb --write
474: npm run agent:replace-proxy -- \
475:   --proxy proxy-id --replacement imported-model-id --shots 08,09,10 \
476:   --output artifacts/refinement/replacement-object.json --write
477: ```
478: 
479: `agent:import-model` calls `window.foreScene.importModel()` and the exact shared
480: engine service used by **Import 3D scene**. It does not create a separate agent
481: asset path. Heavy geometry requires `--allow-heavy-imports`; extreme geometry
482: also requires `--consent-token IMPORT`.
483: 
484: `agent:replace-proxy` gets full shot documents (including direct and keyframe
485: object overrides), creates one atomic plan, renders before evidence, previews,
486: applies, rereads and verifies the project, then renders after evidence. It
487: refuses missing objects, empty/partial shot coverage, failed previews, failed
488: renders, or any project/shot/panorama/camera/timeline verification mismatch. A
489: post-apply failure invokes Agent undo and records that rollback in its JSON
490: report. The report sits beside per-shot `.before.png` and `.after.png` clay
491: frames.
492: 
493: ## Visual CLI
494: 
495: ```bash
496: npm run agent:screenshot -- --workspace shots --output artifacts/shot.png
497: npm run agent:run -- --plan plans/conversation.preview.json --screenshot artifacts/conversation.png --write
498: ```
499: 
500: ## Deferred / not in this milestone
501: 
502: - Selected-keyframe transient staging
503: - `file.import`
504: - `viewport.capture` (screenshots use Playwright against the live canvas today)
505: 
506: ## Autonomous previs (production manifest)
507: 
508: Higher-level graybox pipeline stacked on the Agent API. See `docs/previs-production-manifest.md`.
509: 
510: New browser methods:
511: 
512: - `resetProject({ name, description?, aspectRatio?, frameRate?, expectedProjectId?, resetAuthorization })` — requires read-write **and** `resetAuthorization: "reset-project"`
513: - `getProjectDocument()` — read-only `structuredClone` of the live `LocationProject`
514: 
515: `shot.create` accepts optional `shotNumber` / `productionShotId` so previs shot numbers are preserved exactly.
516: 
517: ```bash
518: npm run agent:previs -- \
519:   --manifest examples/previs/minimal-dialogue.json \
520:   --write --reset-project \
521:   --output artifacts/previs
522: ```
523: ## Missing assets
524: 
525: `foreScene.getStatus()` and `foreScene.inspectProject()` expose `missingAssetCount`. `foreScene.listMissingAssets()` returns each stable asset ID, original filename, resolution status, affected scene instances, and affected shots. With read-write control, `foreScene.relinkAsset({ assetId, file, mode: 'locate' | 'replace' })` reconnects or intentionally replaces the binary without recreating scene objects; `foreScene.removeMissingAsset(assetId)` removes the unresolved asset and its explicit instances. Package export omits missing placeholders and returns warning strings while keeping the project document intact.

(End of file - total 525 lines)
</content>
```

<content>
1: # Production manifest
2: 
3: See also `docs/previs-production-manifest.md` and `src/engine/previs/manifest.ts` in the ForeScene checkout.
4: 
5: Required top-level fields:
6: 
7: - `version: 1`
8: - `project.name`, `project.aspectRatio`
9: - `locations[]` with `id`, `name`, `template`
10: - `cast[]` with either `type: "human_dummy"` or `type: "imported_character"`
11: - `shots[]` with exact `shotNumber`, `name`, `description`, `locationId`, `subjects`, and `camera`
12: 
13: Optional top-level fields are `project.description`, `project.frameRate`, and `props[]`. Optional shot fields are `blocking`, `requirements`, and `motion`.
14: 
15: ## Cast entries
16: 
17: Built-in cast entries use `id`, `name`, and `type: "human_dummy"`. Imported
18: entries use a local source path and rig mode:
19: 
20: ```json
21: {
22:   "id": "lead_actor",
23:   "type": "imported_character",
24:   "source": "./characters/lead-actor.glb",
25:   "rigMode": "preserve-existing"
26: }
27: ```
28: 
29: Imported `name` is optional and defaults to `id`. `source` is resolved relative
30: to the manifest and must be a GLB, embedded glTF, or FBX. Supported
31: `rigMode` values are `preserve-existing`, `auto`, `autorig`, and `saved-rig`. The
32: `agent:previs` cast phase analyzes and imports each declared source in order,
33: persists `cast.<id>` mappings, and only then compiles shots. See
34: [imported-characters.md](imported-characters.md) for recovery guidance.
35: 
36: For an explicit source/package pair, use:
37: 
38: ```json
39: {
40:   "id": "lead_actor",
41:   "type": "imported_character",
42:   "source": "./characters/lead-actor.glb",
43:   "rigMode": "saved-rig",
44:   "rigPackage": "./characters/lead-actor.fsrig"
45: }
46: ```
47: 
48: `rigPackage` is required for `saved-rig` and accepts only `.fsrig` or legacy
49: `.panorig` files. Both paths are resolved relative to the manifest. The pair
50: is checked before reset and the package is applied through the shared saved-rig
51: import path. In a disposable Greenfield manifest-owned project, replacing either
52: file requires `--update-manifest --reset-project`; do not use that reset path to
53: refine an existing project with retained shots or panoramas.
54: 
55: ## Supported enum values
56: 
57: Location templates: `empty_stage`, `interior_room`, `corridor`, `ruins`, `armory`, `exterior_courtyard`, `custom_blueprint`.
58: 
59: Camera templates: `establishing`, `wide`, `full`, `medium`, `medium_close_up`, `close_up`, `extreme_close_up`, `two_shot`, `over_the_shoulder`, `insert`, `profile`, `low_angle`, `high_angle`, `overhead`.
60: 
61: Camera angles: `front`, `three_quarter`, `profile`, `rear`.
62: 
63: Lens classes: `wide`, `normal`, `long`.
64: 
65: Location slots: `center`, `left`, `right`, `foreground`, `background`, `entrance`, `exit`.
66: 
67: Relative relations: `left_of`, `right_of`, `in_front_of`, `behind`, `beside`, `across_from`, `near`, `far_from`, `between`, `just_inside`, `just_outside`.
68: 
69: Do not use `custom_blueprint` unless the current product path explicitly supports it for the run; primitive-template locations are the safer default.
70: 
71: ## Optional shot motion
72: 
73: Use `shots[].motion` for temporal intent:
74: 
75: ```json
76: {
77:   "motion": {
78:     "durationSeconds": 4,
79:     "renderControlVideo": true,
80:     "keyframes": [
81:       {
82:         "timeSeconds": 0,
83:         "camera": {
84:           "position": [0, 2, 6],
85:           "target": [0, 1, 0]
86:         }
87:       },
88:       {
89:         "timeSeconds": 4,
90:         "camera": {
91:           "position": [2, 2, 4],
92:           "target": [0, 1, 0]
93:         },
94:         "staging": [
95:           {
96:             "subject": "alex",
97:             "transform": { "position": [1, 0, 0] },
98:             "posePreset": "walking"
99:           }
100:         ]
101:       }
102:     ]
103:   }
104: }
105: ```
106: 
107: Motion supports `durationSeconds`, optional `renderControlVideo`, and `keyframes`. A keyframe may contain camera `position`, `target`, and `fovDegrees`, plus `staging` entries with `subject`, `visible`, `transform.position`, `transform.rotation`, `transform.scale`, and `posePreset`.
108: 
109: Keyframe constraints:
110: 
111: - At least two keyframes.
112: - `timeSeconds` values strictly increase.
113: - The first keyframe should normally start at `0`.
114: - The final keyframe time must equal `durationSeconds`.
115: - Use as few keyframes as necessary and keep movement semantically meaningful.
116: - `renderControlVideo: true` is for temporal information, not every shot.
117: 
118: See [motion-authoring.md](motion-authoring.md) for coordinate derivation and temporal review.
119: 
120: ## Production-integrity review
121: 
122: Prepared projects should use the gated production workflow described in the
123: main skill and `docs/previs-production-manifest.md`. The runner validates typed

1: # Proxy-to-replacement-object workflow
2: 
3: Use this process when any nonhumanoid final asset replaces an existing proxy. It applies to retained projects; do not reset the project to perform the replacement.
4: 
5: 1. Inspect and record the proxy object ID and every shot that stages or animates it.
6: 2. Import the real GLB and record the resolved real-object ID.
7: 3. Copy the proxy’s base scene transform to the real model.
8: 4. Copy every proxy shot override to the real model.
9: 5. Set the proxy visibility to `false` and real-model visibility to `true` in each affected shot.
10: 6. Copy timeline/keyframe transforms and visibility where applicable.
11: 7. Rerender every affected shot and compare its before/after frames.

1: # Existing-project refinement and preservation
2: 
3: ## Non-destructive default
4: 
5: Select `existing-project-refinement` whenever inspection finds useful geometry, panoramas, shots, cameras, blocking, timelines, or continuity work. The presence of **any** existing shot or panorama prohibits `--reset-project` and `resetProject` unless the user explicitly requests reconstruction. Treat "make it cleaner," "replace the characters," and "update the manifest" as refinement requests, not reset authorization.
6: 
7: ## Required preservation preflight
8: 
9: Before any write, run `npm run agent:inspect -- --url <url>` and capture the full read-only document from `window.foreScene.getProjectDocument()`. Write `artifacts/previs/preflight/project-preservation.json`; it is a required review artifact, not an optional note.
10: 
11: ```json
12: {
13:   "operatingMode": "existing-project-refinement",
14:   "projectId": "project_123",
15:   "projectName": "Existing project",
16:   "preserve": {
17:     "sceneGeometry": true,
18:     "panoramas": true,
19:     "shots": true,
20:     "cameras": true,
21:     "existingTimeline": true
22:   },
23:   "counts": {
24:     "objects": 24,
25:     "panoramas": 2,
26:     "shots": 8
27:   },
28:   "resetAuthorized": false,
29:   "plannedReplacements": [
30:     "placeholder cast model",
31:     "replacement-object proxy",
32:     "environment stand-in"
33:   ],
34:   "preservedIds": {
35:     "shots": ["shot_001", "shot_002"],
36:     "panoramas": ["pano_001", "pano_002"],
37:     "retainedEnvironmentObjects": ["obj_set_wall", "obj_set_door"],
38:     "cameras": ["shot_001:camera", "shot_002:camera"],
39:     "timelineEntries": ["shot_001:keyframe_01", "shot_002:keyframe_01"]
40:   }
41: }
42: ```
43: 
44: Populate the `preservedIds` arrays from the original document, not from guessed names. Record every original shot ID, panorama ID, retained environment-object ID, camera identity, and timeline/keyframe entry. A camera or timeline entry can be represented by a stable composite identifier only when the source document has no separate ID; include its shot ID and original index/keyframe ID so the final check is unambiguous.
45: 
46: `resetAuthorized` may be `true` only when the user explicitly directs reconstruction and the preflight records that direction. It is not authorization to reset an existing project merely because the agent wants a greenfield manifest path.
47: 
48: ## Refinement loop
49: 
50: 1. Retain the full original document snapshot beside the preflight (or in the run record) so transforms, camera data, staging, and timeline state can be compared.
51: 2. Identify the smallest affected shot set. Do not recompile all shots to replace one asset.
52: 3. Analyze/import an asset incrementally, preview the staging plan, then apply it with explicit write access.
53: 4. Work in 3–5-shot batches; render and visually review every affected shot before moving on.
54: 5. Rerender only outputs affected by the changed object, camera, staging, or timeline.
55: 
56: ## Final preservation check
57: 
58: After the last write, read a fresh `getProjectDocument()` snapshot and write `artifacts/previs/preflight/project-preservation-final.json`. It must compare original IDs with final IDs and list any missing or substituted values.
59: 
60: ```json
61: {
62:   "projectId": "project_123",
63:   "passed": true,
64:   "checks": {
65:     "projectIdUnchanged": true,
66:     "shotsRetained": true,
67:     "panoramasRetained": true,
68:     "environmentObjectsRetained": true,
69:     "camerasRetained": true,
70:     "timelineEntriesRetained": true
71:   },
72:   "missingIds": [],
73:   "substitutedIds": [],
74:   "finalCounts": { "objects": 27, "panoramas": 2, "shots": 8 }
75: }
76: ```
77: 
78: The check fails if the project ID changes, any required original ID is missing, a camera/timeline entry was silently replaced, or the preflight cannot establish identity. Do not claim preservation, refinement completion, or production completion until this record passes.

(End of file - total 78 lines)
</content>

1: # Visual acceptance is authoritative
2: 
3: ## Required visual checks
4: 
5: For each final still, compare the opened frame with its shot description. Confirm that:
6: 
7: - The intended primary subject is visible.
8: - The camera frames the intended subject region and composition.
9: - Required scene elements and replacement assets actually appear.
10: - The correct character variant is staged where required.
11: - Required clay, projected, clean-plate, character-only, and depth passes are meaningful and present.
12: 
13: Empty rooms, irrelevant fragments, a missing required scene element, an obscured intended subject, and a proxy counting as the final replacement asset automatically fail. A contact sheet is required for human-readable coverage but never replaces opening suspicious individual frames.
14: 
15: For motion shots, inspect start, midpoint, and endpoint frames and open or sample the MP4. Confirm the motion preserves the intended framing and subject visibility across the move.
16: 
17: ## Evidence hierarchy
18: 
19: File existence does not equal success. Numeric validation is useful for diagnostics but cannot override obvious visual failure.
20: 
21: **When visual evidence conflicts with `validation.json`, trust the visual evidence and mark the shot failed.** Record the conflict and repair plan in the batch review. Do not convert a visual failure to a warning merely because a pixel/statistics or composition record passed.
22: 
23: Do not approve an MP4 from its filename alone. It must be nonempty, associated with the correct shot/pass, sampled or opened, visually accepted, and newer than the last relevant scene change.

(End of file - total 23 lines)
</content>

1: # Gated batch review
2: 
3: ## Batch rule
4: 
5: Use batches of **3–5 shots** by default. Do not autonomously process every shot in a long production after one command succeeds.
6: 
7: For each batch:
8: 
9: 1. Apply only the selected staging, camera, timeline, or asset changes.
10: 2. Render the required review frames and motion samples.
11: 3. Inspect every frame and, for motion, the start, midpoint, endpoint, and opened/sampled MP4.
12: 4. Write `review-manifest.json` and a semantic review using its exact criteria and artifact hashes.
13: 5. Repair every failure and rerender its affected output.
14: 6. Continue only when the batch review has `approved: true` and every required criterion passes.
15: 
16: A failed shot blocks the next batch. A passing command, file existence, or numeric validation alone does not approve a batch.
17: 
18: ```json
19: {
20:   "approved": true,
21:   "manifestSha256": "sha256:...",
22:   "shots": [
23:     {
24:       "id": "shot-id",
25:       "verdict": "pass",
26:       "criteria": [
27:         {
28:           "id": "visual.required-content",
29:           "decision": "pass",
30:           "reason": "All declared shot content is visible in the linked evidence."
31:         }
32:       ],
33:       "reviewedArtifacts": [
34:         { "path": "clay_with_people.png", "sha256": "sha256:..." }
35:       ]
36:     }
37:   ]
38: }
39: ```
40: 
41: ## Required result fields
42: 
43: Each shot result must identify the reviewed output paths and match the
44: manifest’s criteria exactly once. Use `pass`, `fail`, or `not_applicable` only
45: when the criterion definition permits it. Every result needs a concrete
46: reason. Every still and temporal artifact in the manifest must be listed in
47: `reviewedArtifacts` with the matching SHA-256.
48: 
49: If a result is unknown, mark the shot failed until the evidence is inspected.
50: After repair, append or replace the review with a fresh manifest hash and
51: artifact records; do not approve using stale evidence.

55: function createPortableProject(project: LocationProject): LocationProject {

64:   portable.productVersion = portable.productVersion ?? '0.1.0';
65:   for (const asset of Object.values(portable.assets.assets)) {
66:     // Keep inline data URLs until package staging extracts them. Pure migrations
67:     // may assign a planned storageKey without having written binary storage yet.
68:     if (asset.storageKey && !asset.uri.startsWith('data:') && asset.resolutionStatus !== 'missing' && asset.resolutionStatus !== 'corrupt' && asset.resolutionStatus !== 'unsupported') {

72:     }
73:     // Binary skin is the source of truth — never re-embed vertex weight tables.
74:     if (asset.type === 'poseable_rig') {
75:       const rig = asset.metadata?.poseableRig as PoseableRigAsset | undefined;
76:       if (rig) {
77:         const compact = stripInlineSkinArraysFromRig(rig);
78:         if (compact !== rig) {
79:           asset.metadata = {
80:             ...asset.metadata,
81:             poseableRig: compact,
82:           };
83:         }
84:       }
85:     }
86:   }
87:   return portable;

107:   const migrated = new Map<string, Blob>();
108:   for (const asset of Object.values(project.assets.assets)) {
109:     if (!isRasterOrVideoAsset(asset) || !asset.uri.startsWith('data:')) continue;
110:     const storageKey = storageKeyForAsset(project, asset);
111:     const blob = dataUrlToBlob(asset.uri);
112:     migrated.set(storageKey, blob);

120: async function hydrateProjectAssetUris(project: LocationProject): Promise<LocationProject> {
121:   const writes: Array<{ key: string; blob: Blob }> = [];
122:   for (const asset of Object.values(project.assets.assets)) {
123:     if (!isRasterOrVideoAsset(asset)) continue;

129:       continue;
130:     }
131:     const storageKey = portableStorageKey(asset);
132:     if (storageKey) asset.storageKey = storageKey;
133:   }
134:   await putProjectAssetBlobs(writes);

136:   for (const asset of Object.values(project.assets.assets)) {

138:     const uri = await resolveProjectAssetUri(asset);
139:     if (!uri) throw new Error(`Project package is missing binary asset ${asset.name}.`);

215:   if (params.reviewRequiredShotIds.length > 0) return 'needs_review';
216:   if (params.warnings > 0) return 'completed_with_warnings';

249: /** Enforces an optional wall-clock budget across production phases. */
250: export class ProductionTimeBudget {
251:   private readonly deadlineMs: number;
252: 
253:   constructor(seconds: number, startedAt = Date.now()) {
254:     this.deadlineMs = startedAt + seconds * 1000;
255:   }
256: 
257:   remainingMs(): number {
258:     return Math.max(0, this.deadlineMs - Date.now());
259:   }
260: 
261:   isExpired(): boolean {
262:     return this.remainingMs() <= 0;
263:   }
264: 
265:   assertWithinBudget(phase: string): void {
266:     if (this.isExpired()) {
267:       throw new ProductionTimeBudgetExceededError(phase);
268:     }
269:   }
270: }

272: export function hasMissingControlVideos(params: {

275:   skipControlVideos: boolean;

280:     const shotState = params.shotStates[shot.shotNumber];

168:     const width = header.readUInt32BE(16);

515:     const result = await window.foreScene!.importCharacter({
516:       analysisId: analysis.analysisId,
517:       mode,
518:       name: input.name,
519:       consentToken: input.consentToken,
520:     });
521:     return { analysis, result };
522:   }, {
523:     name: entry.character.name,
524:     height: entry.character.height,
525:     rigMode: entry.character.rigMode,
526:     consentToken,
527:   });
528:   return { sourcePath, result };
529: }

531: async function analyzeManifestSavedRigCharacter(
532:   page: Page,
533:   asset: ResolvedManifestCharacterAsset,
534:   character: Extract<PrevisProductionManifestV1['cast'][number], { type: 'imported_character' }>,
535: ) {
536:   if (!asset.rigPackagePath) throw new Error(`No rig package was resolved for saved-rig character "${character.id}".`);
537:   await page.locator('[data-agent-character-import-input]').setInputFiles(asset.sourcePath);
538:   await page.locator('[data-agent-character-rig-package-input]').setInputFiles(asset.rigPackagePath);
539:   return page.evaluate(async (input) => {
540:     const sourceInput = document.querySelector('[data-agent-character-import-input]') as HTMLInputElement | null;
541:     const rigInput = document.querySelector('[data-agent-character-rig-package-input]') as HTMLInputElement | null;
542:     const sourceFile = sourceInput?.files?.[0];
543:     const rigPackageFile = rigInput?.files?.[0];
544:     if (!sourceFile || !rigPackageFile) throw new Error('Saved-rig files were not staged in the browser.');
545:     const sourceAnalysis = await window.foreScene!.analyzeCharacterImport({
546:       file: sourceFile,
547:       mode: 'auto',
548:       ...(input.height !== undefined ? { approximateHeightMeters: input.height } : {}),
549:     });
550:     const compatibility = await window.foreScene!.analyzeSavedRigCharacter({
551:       sourceFile,
552:       rigPackageFile,
553:       ...(input.height !== undefined ? { approximateHeightMeters: input.height } : {}),
554:     });
555:     return { ...compatibility, sourceImportRequiresConsent: sourceAnalysis.requiresConsent };
556:   }, { height: character.height });
557: }

562:   character: Extract<PrevisProductionManifestV1['cast'][number], { type: 'imported_character' }>,
563:   consentToken?: string,
564: ) {
565:   if (!asset.rigPackagePath) throw new Error(`No rig package was resolved for saved-rig character "${character.id}".`);
566:   await page.locator('[data-agent-character-import-input]').setInputFiles(asset.sourcePath);
567:   await page.locator('[data-agent-character-rig-package-input]').setInputFiles(asset.rigPackagePath);
568:   return page.evaluate(async (input) => {
569:     const sourceInput = document.querySelector('[data-agent-character-import-input]') as HTMLInputElement | null;
570:     const rigInput = document.querySelector('[data-agent-character-rig-package-input]') as HTMLInputElement | null;
571:     const sourceFile = sourceInput?.files?.[0];
572:     const rigPackageFile = rigInput?.files?.[0];

574:     return window.foreScene!.importSavedRigCharacter({
575:       sourceFile,
576:       rigPackageFile,
577:       name: input.name,
578:       consentToken: input.consentToken,
